items.q: Where does Kanoski put meal memory?
items.a: In the **hippocampus**, fed by gut signals. Natural **GLP-1** comes from intestinal L cells and from the **brainstem**. The hippocampus has many **GLP-1 receptors**. Gut GLP-1 acts in part on **vagus** terminals.

items.q: What did early sugar access do in his animals?
items.a: Free access to a solution at about a **soft drink’s** calorie share, with otherwise healthy food. **Hippocampal deficits** show up when they are older and **persist after the sugar stops**. He ties some of that to **microbiome** changes.

items.q: What is the Western diet on this tape?
items.a: About **35 percent** of calories from fat and **15 percent** from **simple sugar**, in adult animals. Junk food (peanut-butter cups, chips, a high-fat high-sugar diet) leaves impairments that **last after a switch to healthy food**.

items.q: What is the last step into the hippocampus?
items.a: **Acetylcholine** neurons in the **medial septum**, reached from the brainstem. That is the three-tier path he draws from the gut to meal memory.
